courses.title: Ethics and Critical Thinking
courses.description: A foundational course exploring ethical theory and critical thinking in ministry contexts. Students examine moral frameworks and develop analytical skills.
courses.overview: This course introduces students to fundamental principles of ethics and develops critical thinking abilities essential for leadership and ministry.
learningOutcomes: Understand core ethical frameworks and theories
Apply critical thinking to real-world scenarios
courses.whoIsFor: All Bachelor's degree students seeking foundational ethical training
courses.format: Lectures, discussions, case studies, and written reflections

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Fundamental skills in conducting academic research within theological contexts. Learn quantitative and qualitative research methodologies.
courses.overview: Students develop proficiency in research design, data collection, analysis, and presentation of findings in academic and professional settings.
courses.whoIsFor: Students pursuing advanced degrees or research-focused careers
courses.format: Seminars, workshops, lab work, and research projects

courses.title: History of Christianity and World Religions
courses.description: A comprehensive examination of Christian history and comparative study of world religions. Explores theological development and interfaith dialogue.
courses.overview: This master's level course provides deep historical context for Christianity and explores major world religious traditions to enhance interfaith understanding.
learningOutcomes: Trace major developments in Christian history
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor's degree and admission to Master's program
courses.whoIsFor: Master's students in Ministry, Theology, or Religious Studies

courses.title: Substance Use and Public Health
courses.description: Examination of substance use disorders from a public health perspective. Covers epidemiology, prevention, treatment, and policy implications.
courses.overview: Students develop comprehensive understanding of substance use as a public health issue, including prevention strategies and evidence-based interventions.
courses.whoIsFor: Public health, counseling, and healthcare students

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Foundational course covering basic computer science concepts, programming fundamentals, and computational thinking.
courses.overview: Introduction to algorithms, data representation, problem-solving strategies, and basic programming concepts using modern languages.
courses.whoIsFor: All students interested in computer science and programming

courses.title: Principles of Business Administration
courses.description: Comprehensive overview of business fundamentals including management, marketing, finance, and organizational behavior.
courses.overview: An introductory course covering core business disciplines and their integration in modern organizations.
courses.whoIsFor: Business majors and students seeking business literacy

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description: Foundational exploration of psychology including biological, cognitive, social, and developmental perspectives on human behavior.
courses.overview: Students develop understanding of psychological principles and their applications to individual and social behavior.
courses.whoIsFor: All students interested in psychology and human behavior

courses.title: Drawing I: Observational Foundations
courses.description: Foundational drawing course emphasizing observation skills, composition, and fundamental techniques.
courses.overview: Students develop essential drawing skills through study of light, shadow, proportion, and perspective.
courses.whoIsFor: Art majors and students seeking creative expression

courses.title: College Composition I
courses.college: College of Education and Human Development
courses.description: Introduction to college-level writing with emphasis on essay structure, argumentation, and research skills.
courses.overview: Students develop strong foundational writing skills essential for academic success across all disciplines.
courses.whoIsFor: All students requiring college writing skills

courses.title: Foundations of Business and Management
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to business management for graduate students. Covers organizational theory, strategy, and leadership fundamentals.
courses.overview: This course provides advanced understanding of business principles and management practices in contemporary organizations.
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor's degree and admission to MBA program

courses.title: Foundations of Faith
courses.description: Introduction to Christian faith and theology. Explores biblical foundations, core doctrines, and Christian traditions.
courses.overview: Students develop foundational understanding of Christian belief, practice, and theology.
courses.whoIsFor: Seminary students and students of Christian faith
